The question of whether Tesla invented radio is genuinely contested. The majority of retrieved sources credit Tesla as the true inventor of radio, citing his 1893 public demonstration of radio principles [d4][d11], his radio patent applications filed in 1897 and granted in 1900 [d1][d6][d12], and the 1943 U.S. Supreme Court ruling that invalidated Marconi's radio patents in favor of Tesla (and others) [d3][d5][d7]. The Patent Office itself repeatedly rejected Marconi's applications, noting that "many of the claims are not patentable over Tesla patent numbers 645,576 and 649,621" [d1][d6], and CNN notes that Marconi's transatlantic transmission relied on 17 of Tesla's patents [d7]. However, d10 explicitly labels Tesla's invention of radio a "myth," arguing that Russian physicist Alexander Popov demonstrated a working radio receiver in 1895, predating both Tesla and Marconi, and that the invention was a collective achievement built on many prior scientists' work [d10]. Meanwhile, d9 and d13 note that Marconi is more commonly credited because he successfully commercialized the technology, even if his work was heavily based on Tesla's [d9][d13]. In sum, while Tesla has strong legal and historical claims to priority over Marconi, the broader question of who "invented" radio remains a matter of genuine debate, with some sources pointing to even earlier contributors [d10].
